Dropping the second product's logo write leaves that field at whatever default the editor started with, instead of "b.png" — the equivalence test compares the fast path's saved brief against the typed path's byte for byte, so a skipped field must fail it, not pass silently through a partial draft that happens to still be structurally valid.

mutations.because: Qodo's finding on this PR: setField's job is not only to reach the same draft, it must also leave the same interaction state the typed path leaves — in particular, the last field focused. Dropping el.focus() (the only thing in setField that ever moves document.activeElement — fireEvent.click and fireEvent.change do not) leaves nothing focused after fillValidDraft returns, instead of the second product's Logo Path the typed path leaves focused. The draft itself is unaffected (this mutation cannot fail the byte-for-byte body comparison), so only the focus-equivalence assertion catches it — proving that assertion pins something the draft comparison alone cannot see.

note:
A fourth candidate mutation — drop `fireEvent.click(el)` (leave `.focus()` and `fireEvent.change`) — was tried and does NOT fail the touched-sections assertion in this test: `fillValidDraft` always clicks the real 'Add product' button (an unconverted `user.click`, unchanged by this lane) before either path fills the second product's fields, and that click alone already marks the Products section touched regardless of whether the individual field writes click first. So this specific assertion cannot isolate the per-field click's own contribution for the Products section — and Identity and Copy have no available candidate at all, since every field they contain is also directly field-touched by its own blur, which already satisfies visibleErrors' gate on its own. Recorded honestly rather than manufacturing a mutation this test does not, in fact, catch (the same discipline X30's and X32's manifests already applied to their own declined slots). The click is kept in setField anyway, on structural grounds: it is what the real typed path does before every keystroke, and it is what actually changes `touchedSections` for a differently-shaped fillValidDraft call in the future, even where this file's current fields cannot expose the difference today.

A fifth candidate was considered for the isolation fix itself (the nested `describe` and the `try`/`finally` around `beforeAll`/`observeFillValidDraft`) and no mutation is recorded for it, honestly rather than by omission: this manifest's mechanism checks one command's exit code per mutation (caught = nonzero, survived = zero), scoped by `-t` to the one test each entry names. What the isolation fix protects against is a DIFFERENT test — a sibling in the parent describe — being skipped or failed as a side effect of this one's `beforeAll` throwing. Expressing that would need a mutation that both (a) reverts the nested `describe` (puts `beforeAll` back in the parent scope) AND (b) makes the reference build throw, then runs the WHOLE FILE (no `-t`) and checks that MORE than one test's outcome changed — a shape this tool cannot state (its exit code is binary per command, not a count or a set of which tests were affected). Manually reproduced instead (recorded in the PR that added this fix): forcing `typeFillValidDraftByHand` to throw skips exactly the one equivalent test (`↓`) and leaves all 181 others — including the four tests X30/X32/X34 exist to rescue — passing, with the render `try`/`finally` unmounting on the failure path and the `beforeAll` `try`/`finally` restoring the `fetch` spy and clearing `localStorage` so nothing leaks into the next test. That is a fact about this fix, verified by hand, not a claim this manifest can carry as a caught mutation.
